As the southwest monsoon pulls back, initial hot and humid conditions in Mumbai intensified into isolated heat-wave warnings, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), with weather officials issuing yellow alerts across several districts of Maharashtra, specifically Thane,
According to the Met department, in Mumbai, hot weather conditions escalated on Friday, October 9, 2026, with dry weather expected to follow for the remainder of the forecast period. Raigad is experiencing similar weather initially, followed by isolated heat-wave conditions and a subsequent return to warm weather, IMD said.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a Yellow Alert (Watch - Be Aware) for Day 2, expanding coverage along the western belt to include Palghar, Thane, Mumbai, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Kolhapur and its ghats, Satara and its ghats, Sangli, and Sholapur.
On Saturday, October 10, 2026, the yellow alert narrows to select coastal, southern, and ghat districts, specifically Thane, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Kolhapur, the Ghats of Kolhapur, the Ghats of Satara, and Sangli. By Day 4, Sunday, October 11 and Day 5, Monday, October 12, conditions are expected to normalise completely, with green warnings (no adverse weather action required) returning across the entire state of Maharashtra, IMD said.
The weather patterns are also drawing examination from economic analysts tracking agricultural risks. Weighing in on the macro outlook from Mumbai, CRISIL Chief Economist Dharmakirti Joshi noted that upside risks remain prevalent on the food inflation front.
"The inflation risk from the food side is tilted to the upside," Joshi said.
He added, "In that scenario, you'll have to wait and see because El Nino intensifying means there is a possibility of further disruptions from the weather side, which could have implications for crops and inflation also."

articles.full_text:
Bhubaneswar: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow warning for 13 districts of Odisha, forecasting thunderstorms, lightning and rainfall as the southwest monsoon continues its withdrawal from the state.
According to the weather forecast, isolated areas in the districts covered by the warning may experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 30–40 kmph. Residents have been advised to remain cautious during adverse weather conditions.
The warning comes at a time when the southwest monsoon is gradually retreating from Odisha. Despite the withdrawal process, local weather conditions may still trigger thunderstorms and rainfall in several parts of the state.
Monsoon Retreat Advances Across Odisha
The southwest monsoon began withdrawing from Odisha on Thursday, with the process covering most parts of Bargarh district and some areas of Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Balangir, Nuapada and Nabarangpur districts.

The changing weather pattern signals a gradual transition away from the monsoon season. The IMD has indicated that conditions are favourable for the monsoon to withdraw from additional parts of eastern India over the next few days.
Residents Advised to Stay Alert During Thunderstorms
Although the monsoon is retreating, the possibility of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds remains in the districts under the yellow warning. People are advised to follow official weather updates and take precautions during lightning activity, particularly by avoiding open fields and exposed locations.
The IMD has not issued a weather warning for any Odisha district for Saturday, October 10, according to the report. Residents are encouraged to monitor subsequent forecasts for any changes in weather conditions.

articles.full_text:
Thiruvananthapuram, 09 Oct (H.S.): Heavy rain is likely across parts of Kerala on Friday and Saturday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing yellow alerts for nine districts on Friday and four on Saturday.
Friday’s alerts cover Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod. On Saturday, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam and Idukki will remain under yellow alert.
The department defines heavy rainfall as precipitation ranging from 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm within 24 hours. The forecast also warns of thunderstorms, lightning and winds reaching speeds of 40–50 kmph during the two days.
Several weather systems are contributing to the rainfall, according to the department. A cyclonic circulation persists over the southeastern Arabian Sea near the southern Kerala coast, at an altitude of 5.8 km above sea level.
Another cyclonic circulation is located over northern Tamil Nadu at the same altitude. A trough extends from the Gulf of Mannar to central Maharashtra through Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, at 0.9 km above sea level. The combined influence of these systems is bringing rain to Kerala, the department said.
Meanwhile, the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has warned of coastal inundation along parts of the Thiruvananthapuram and Kanniyakumari coasts because of the “kallakkadal” phenomenon, involving swell waves.
Along the Thiruvananthapuram coastline, from Kappil to Pozhiyoor, waves measuring between 0.9 and 1.1 metres could cause seawater to surge ashore until 11.30 p.m. on Friday.
A warning is in place for the Kanniyakumari coast, where waves ranging from 0.9 to 1.3 metres could trigger coastal inundation during the same period.
The coastal warnings accompany the rainfall forecast, with southern coastal areas facing possible wave-related impacts while several districts remain under alerts for heavy rain. The advisories identify separate risks from rainfall, thunderstorms, strong winds and sea conditions during the forecast period.

articles.full_text:
Mumbai Weather Update: City Braces for 38°C Heat as Air Quality Remains Unhealthy
By Lokmat Times Desk | Updated: October 9, 2026 14:15 IST2026-10-09T14:14:28+5:302026-10-09T14:15:37+5:30
Mumbai is set to experience hot and humid conditions on Friday, with clear skies expected through the day. The weather department has warned of heatwave conditions in isolated areas, while rising pollution levels remain a concern.
Mumbai woke up to hot and humid conditions on Friday, October 9, with temperatures expected to reach around 38°C, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The city recorded a minimum temperature of 29°C in the morning and is likely to experience largely clear skies throughout the day. The IMD has issued a heatwave warning for isolated pockets of Mumbai and Raigad, marking the first heatwave warning of the post-monsoon season. High humidity is expected to add to the discomfort as temperatures rise during the afternoon.
IMD Issues Heatwave Warning for Isolated Areas
According to the IMD, temperatures in isolated parts of Mumbai and Raigad are expected to remain several degrees above normal. Residents may experience particularly uncomfortable conditions during the afternoon as the mercury rises. The weather department has also forecast hot and humid conditions at isolated locations in neighbouring Thane and Palghar.

Mumbai AQI Stands at 153
Mumbai recorded an overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of 153 on Friday, according to official data. The reading indicates a deterioration in air quality compared with the relatively better levels recorded across the city in recent months. The combination of high temperatures, humidity and elevated pollution levels is likely to add to the discomfort for residents.
What Does an AQI of 153 Mean?
Under the AQI classification cited in the report, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as 'Good', 51 to 100 as 'Moderate', 101 to 200 as 'Unhealthy', 201 to 300 as 'Poor', and readings above 300 as 'Severe'. Mumbai's reading of 153 falls within the 101 to 200 category, highlighting concerns over the city's air quality alongside the hot and humid weather.
